question: Find the midpoint of segment joining (3,4) and (7,8).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The coordinates of the midpoint are the simple average of the given x and y coordinates.

x-coordinate = (3 + 7) ÷ 2 = 5

y-coordinate = (4 + 8) ÷ 2 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is (5, 6).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First point (x₁, y₁) = (3, 4)

Second point (x₂, y₂) = (7, 8)

**Formula Used:**

Midpoint Formula: M(x, y) = ((x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2, (y₁ + y₂) ÷ 2)

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 A (3, 4)
 B (7, 8)
 M (x, y)

**Calculation:**

⇒ x-coordinate = (3 + 7) ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5

⇒ y-coordinate = (4 + 8) ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6

⇒ The midpoint is (5, 6).

**∴ The correct answer is (5, 6).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Distance Formula

The distance d between two points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is given by d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).

Section Formula

A point P(x, y) dividing a line segment joining two points internally in the ratio m:n has coordinates x = (mx₂ + nx₁) ÷ (m + n) and y = (my₂ + ny₁) ÷ (m + n).

Centroid of a Triangle

The centroid coordinates of a triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂) and (x₃, y₃) are given by ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃) ÷ 3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) ÷ 3).
